extDescription.message: Reveal this QR Code - decode QR images on any page and inspect the payload before you trust it.
extDescription.description: Extension description, shown in the browser and in the store listing.

uiBadgeReveal.description: Caption on the badge that appears over a decoded QR image.

uiBadgeAllow.description: Caption on the badge shown over an image deQR is not permitted to read.

uiBadgeAllowTitle.message: deQR cannot read this image because it is served from $origin$ without CORS headers. Click to grant access to that origin.

uiDialogLabel.description: Accessible name of the reveal panel.

uiDestination.description: Label above the hostname the browser will really resolve.

uiDisplaysAs.description: The hostname as it looks, when that differs from what resolves.

uiShow.description: Button that reveals a masked secret such as a Wi-Fi password.

uiTruncated.description: Note under a payload too long to print in full.

uiOpenAnyway.description: Open button for a payload that carries a warning.

uiOpenConfirm.description: Armed state of the Open button; the second click navigates.

uiWillNotOpen.message: deQR will not open this. Copy the text if you need to inspect it.

optImageAccessHelp.message: deQR reads QR codes out of the page itself and needs no special access for images hosted by the site you are visiting. Images served from another origin without CORS headers cannot be read at all - the browser blocks it. Add those origins here to let deQR fetch them directly. Nothing is sent anywhere; the fetch happens locally in your browser.

optDeepScanHelp.message: Send every image to the decoder instead of pre-screening for QR finder patterns first. Catches blurred, skewed, and photographed codes that the fast filter misses. Noticeably slower on image-heavy pages.

optRevealSecretsHelp.message: Wi-Fi passwords and two-factor seeds are hidden behind a click by default, so they are not exposed to anyone looking at your screen.

optAppearanceHelp.message: Applies to this page and to the reveal panel deQR opens over a page. Open tabs pick up a change straight away.

optThemeSystemHelp.message: Follow whatever your operating system is set to.

optDisabledSitesHelp.message: deQR does not scan pages on these hostnames.

optFooter.message: deQR decodes entirely on your machine. It makes no network requests of its own, sends no telemetry, and never transmits a decoded payload.

optInvalidOrigin.message: That is not a valid origin.

optOnlyHttp.message: Only http and https origins can be granted.

payloadCrypto.description: Panel heading for a cryptocurrency payment. The network name is a proper noun and is never translated.

fieldEmvAccount.description: EMVCo payment account. The tag is a two-digit number from the spec.

fieldVerbatim.description: A field name taken straight from the payload, such as an unrecognized vCard tag. Nothing to translate.

valueSecurityNone.description: Wi-Fi security type when the network is open.

valueAmountUnset.message: not fixed - set by the payer

reasonBlockedSchemeDetail.message: This is not a web address. Opening it would run code or read a local resource in your browser. deQR will not open it.

reasonUserinfoTitle.message: The visible domain is not where this goes

reasonUserinfoDetail.message: Everything before the "@" is ignored by the browser. This link resolves to $host$, not to $shown$.

reasonUserinfoDetailUnnamed.message: Everything before the "@" is ignored by the browser. This link resolves to $host$, not to the name shown first.
reasonUserinfoDetailUnnamed.description: Used when the part before the @ has no readable name to quote back.

reasonMixedScriptDetail.message: The hostname reads as "$host$", which combines $scripts$ characters. Real domains almost never do this; lookalike domains do. The browser will resolve it as $ascii$.

reasonConfusableTitle.message: Domain uses letters that imitate Latin ones

reasonConfusableDetail.message: Characters in this hostname look like ordinary letters but are not. The browser will resolve it as $ascii$. If you expected an all-Latin address, this is not it.

reasonPunycodeDetail.message: Resolves to $ascii$. Verify this is the domain you expect.

reasonInsecureDetail.message: Anything you send to this page can be read and modified in transit.

reasonShortenerDetail.message: $domain$ forwards somewhere else. Nothing in this QR code tells you where.

reasonIpHostTitle.message: Numeric address instead of a domain name

reasonIpHostDetail.message: Legitimate services are normally reached by domain name.

reasonPortDetail.message: Web services rarely ask you to connect on an unusual port.

reasonNestedUrlDetail.message: $host$ is only the first hop. The "$param$" parameter sends you to: $target$

reasonLongUrlDetail.message: $count$ characters. Length is often used to push the real domain out of view.

reasonTotpSeedTitle.message: This is a two-factor authentication seed

reasonTotpSeedDetail.message: Scanning this with an authenticator app gives that app a permanent code generator for the account. If you did not just ask a service to enrol a new authenticator, do not use it.

reasonWifiDetail.message: Whoever runs the network can see and alter unencrypted traffic. Only join networks you know.

reasonPaymentDetail.message: Check the recipient and amount below against the merchant you are actually dealing with. These transfers are normally irreversible, and swapping the payment QR is a common scam.

reasonPremiumRateDetail.message: $number$ matches a premium-rate prefix. Calls or messages to these numbers can be charged at a high rate.

reasonPrefilledSmsTitle.message: Sends a pre-written message on your behalf

reasonPrefilledSmsDetail.message: Read the message text below before sending. Premium shortcodes bill on receipt.

reasonGroupInviteDetail.message: Joining shows your phone number and profile to everyone already in the group, and there is no way to tell from the invite who that is.

reasonPrefilledWhatsappTitle.message: Opens a chat with a pre-written message

reasonPrefilledWhatsappDetail.message: Both the recipient and the message text were chosen by whoever made this QR code. Check the number below - starting the chat reveals your number to it.

reasonPrefilledMailDetail.message: The message body was chosen by whoever made this QR code, not by you.

reasonBidiDetail.message: Invisible characters that reorder how text is displayed. They are used to make a hostile address read as a harmless one. They have been removed from the text shown here.

reasonZeroWidthDetail.message: Zero-width characters are present. They cannot be seen but change what the text actually is.
